sql_schemas: table leave_types | fields: id, name, description, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: name: unique lookup by leave type name (annual, sick, emergency, etc.); is_active: filter active leave types in dropdowns and policy assignment

table leave_policies | fields: id, policy_name, leave_type_id, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: leave_type_id -> leave_types.id | indexes: leave_type_id: join with leave_types for policy lookups by type; is_active: filter active policies during leave application validation

table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_id, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_id -> leave_types.id; approved_by -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: list own leave requests; join to employee; status: filter by status for approval queues and dashboards; leave_type_id: filter requests by leave type; start_date, end_date: date-range overlap detection and calendar views; approved_by: manager approval queue lookups

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, leave_type_id, policy_id, fiscal_year, total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_type_id -> leave_types.id; policy_id -> leave_policies.id | indexes: employee_id: look up balance for a specific employee; employee_id, fiscal_year: unique balance per employee per fiscal year; frequent composite lookup; leave_type_id: filter balances by leave type; policy_id: join to policy for entitlement rules

table employees | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_number: unique lookup by employee number; email: unique lookup by email; manager_id: team hierarchy queries for approval chains; employment_status: filter active employees; department: group employees by department

table audit_logs | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, old_values, new_values, performed_by, performed_at, ip_address, user_agent, created_at | pk: id | indexes: entity_type, entity_id: look up audit trail for a specific entity; performed_by: filter audit records by actor; action: filter by action type (CREATE, UPDATE, APPROVE, REJECT); performed_at: time-range queries for audit reports

table notifications | fields: id, recipient_id, type, title, message, related_entity_type, related_entity_id, status, created_at, read_at | pk: id | fks: recipient_id -> employees.id | indexes: recipient_id: list notifications for a user; status: filter unread/pending notifications; related_entity_type, related_entity_id: find notifications linked to a specific leave request
data_notes: All tables are conceptual specs only — no SQL DDL. The employees, audit_logs, and notifications tables are referenced by the leave module's FK relationships and are defined here once. Repositories use PostgreSQL via the existing pg Pool at src/shared/db/connection.ts. Every state-changing operation on leave_requests and leave_balances must write an audit_logs row per GP-002. The leave_requests.status field uses the LeaveStatus enum values (DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED). The leave_balances table tracks per-employee, per-leave-type, per-fiscal-year balances with atomic deductDays/restoreDays methods to prevent race conditions during concurrent approvals.
